column4: Tasting Notes

One of our core values here at Altitude is having a good time. Some days are naturally gonna be better than others, and some don't go as planned, but as they say, you can turn lemons into lemonade. When it's time to pass up a beer, we respect that. But it never means you shouldn't be having a good time as good times are all the time with us. This extra pale ale is crafted with all the best qualities of a full-flavoured brew but without the booze.

column3: Jam Sessions Vol. 3: Boysenberry, Blackberry & Raspberry (Nitro)
column4: Reissued. Welcome back to the third jam session in our ongoing series, featuring a trio of wicked berries. This session started with a creamy kettle-soured base that's been fermented really clean. Then we kept hitting it layers of hand-selected fruits until we reached the pitch-perfect harmony of tart, sweet, creamy and refreshing. Store chilled for the freshest performance.

This is the quintessential brewer's beer. A classic style that is uncomplicated and easy to drink, but the exact opposite when it comes to the brewing. Endless careful practice, recipe crafting and flawless production technique are all that is needed to produce a full-flavoured and well-balanced Helles. Something that would make a proud Bavarian as happy to drink it as we are happy making it.

After making one delicious beer with our mates over in WA, the thirsty world demanded another. This time they came to us for a brew day, and we have created another classic for those demanding dry mouths. Hang time is a punchy, full-bodied hazy using the goodness of 2 hops we have never used before in NZ 101 and Alora. This NZ/US combo delivers passion and stone fruit to the moon that is backed up with tingly yuzu and lime zest and some sweet melon smooches.

column3: You Can Call Me Al (Aliment Collab)
column4: Hi, my name is Al. I am the very special progeny of a collaboration between breweries Altitude and Aliment. I would like to tell you a bit about myself. I am beautiful dark bronze, fresh espresso colour with a soft tan foam on top. First impressions aside, you should smell my delicious top notes of baked rye sourdough, toasted caramel nuts, sticky toffee pudding and hints of dried fruits. If this doesn't make you love me, then I taste just as good. An Initial rich toasted fruit bread flavour is superseded by a little chocolate note, with a full yet very clean mouthfeel from my lager fermentation.

Brewed for the 2026 WC IPA challenge, this year's entry is Jazz hands; The iconic, inspirational, and awesome time-honoured move that's synonymous with the stage. Don't let it be your Mr Cellophane and pass you by at this year's challenge or any other event. Pungent aromas of fresh sticky buds, key lime pie and blackberry crumble layer up into a hop-saturated mouthfeel that jazz's hard. Dry and refined, the bitterness hits early, right with the saturation of flavour and ends the performance perfectly in the West Coast (end) stage, wanting an encore.

Queenstown's hottest summer beverage is back.  This insanely popular concoction is summer in a glass: a fresh and zesty sparkling white sangria with a beautiful pink blush that's poured over ice. 2026 edition brings a classic combo of strawberry and lime to the sangria table. Juicy spring strawberry aromas meld with fresh grape and a light, dry spritzy mouthfeel, with a fresh citrus edge that quenches all thirsts.

When you unwrap this box of chocolates, you know exactly what you're gonna get. Brewed to capture the unmistakable indulgence of a chocolate hazelnut truffle, this indulgent beer pours deep black with notes of Nutella, roasted hazelnuts, Belgian chocolate and espresso. Full-bodied and velvety with a lingering milk chocolate sweetness that is balanced by an easy and mild roasted bitterness.

A decadent pastry stout inspired by the classic German chocolate cake, pouring deep obsidian with a creamy mocha head. Rich aromas of dark chocolate brownie, toasted coconut and fresh roast coffee rise from the glass. The palate layers velvety cocoa, caramelised sugar, creamy coconut and subtle vanilla frosting. All this indulgence is balanced by a subtle earthy bitterness and a touch of roast. Full-bodied and dessert-like without becoming cloying, it finishes clean enough to enjoy another bite.

column3: Fin the beer Main character energy

column4:
We at Behemoth believe in bigger tasting beers; big on flavour and fun! This is why the majority of our beers have big percentages and big full-body flavours. But we're also not afraid to try something new...

So! We are releasing Responsibly Non-Alcoholic Hazy IPA with all the flavour you want when reaching for a beer at the end of the day! Made with Pale Malt, Vienna Malt, Oats, Wheat and Carahell Malts along with Citra, Mosaic, Galaxy, and Riwaka Hops to give you an incredibly flavourful and refreshing Hazy IPA just without the booze!
Brewed with our mates at the Black Seeds. It is a hazy loaded with real watermelon from Vietnam, it is one for real watermelon lovers, watermelon in beer form.
Just like your classic frozen margarita but made with a citrus sour beer base!
Like your favourite frozen margarita but made with a sour mango beer base!

Brewed with our mates at Brothers for Auckland Beer Week we used Riwaka, citra and Motueka hop flakes. Along with a little bit of rice in the grain bill to lighten the body and make it that much more drinkable.
This hazy is here to showcase brand new American Dolcita hops showcasing vibrant notes of candied peach rings, pineapple, tangerine, and sweet cream.
Small lager yeast fermented stout with the taste of Agave. The warming taste of Mexico right here at Beervana.

Churly's has been nice enough to give his share back into this stout which we had agreed on Oak Staves that have held whiskies from around the world. Now you can get the taste of your favourite dram in this smooth, flavourful and maybe far too easy drinking tropical stout.

Back in 2012 a brewery called Green Flash from San Diego created what may be the hoppiest beer in the world at the time. This is our ode to that beer. 9 ALC/VOL and 250 theoretical IBUs (because your taste buds struggle to register anything over 100 IBU but we wanted to give it a crack). Bitter beers may have fallen out of fashion, but we have loaded this beer with Columbus, Moutere, Centennial, Nelson Sauvin and Cryo Simcoe to give you a full on assault to the senses—so many hops it will weaken even the most sturdy wooden pallet!
A slightly sweet sparkling session mead made from multi-flora mānuka honey fermented with Ruapehu mountain water.
The familiar flavours of your favourite apple pie. Crisp apple, cinnamon and a hint of ginger.
The natural sweetness of New Zealand’s bush honey paired with fresh and sour cherry juice.
Subtle hints of honey with a ginger spicy aftertaste. Tastes like the sweet spot between ginger beer and ginger ale.
A crisp, semi-dry co-ferment of apple and peach, dry hopped with Nectaron hops from NZ Hops to deliver tropical and stone fruit aromatics and a clean, refreshing finish.
Cutting through the crap. A clean, refreshing lager to cleanse your palate.

A delightfully bright and refreshing sour made with a heap of NZ's favourite winter fruit. There is a small addition of salt and coriander for some complexity (you're welcome beer nerds) , but the feijoa is undoubtedly the star of the show.
A tangy, tart rollercoaster of flavour. Fruited with a heap of guava, orange, banana, feijoa, strawberry and a little vanilla. A sour beer, that doesn't taste like beer at all.
Our flagship hazy. Fruity, tropical, smooth and delicious.
A punchy and clean WCIPA, with a big hop dose of Citra, Nelson Sauvin and NZ Cascade. TBC
Our NZ Stout Challenge 2026 entry. A silky, rich stout enhanced with orange slices, vanilla. and a variety of delicious warming spices. Mulled Stout, if you will

“Hazesteria is what they've called it” said a bearded beer geek. 

The crowd grew. 

“My friend’s friend works with a guy that knows the brewer” said a girl wearing Docs “and he says they used loads of Mosaic and Nectaron in the dry hop!”

A chant began: “Hazy! Hazy! Hazy! HAZY!” 

Super smashable, with notes of mango, stone fruits, lime and citrus.

Relaaax, dude. You're like,  totally here now, y'know? You can just sit back and soak in the vibes, like a happy lil' beer dude.  This bodacious NZ Pils, it's like totally limey and stuff, just super crisp. Like, it's got Motueka, and Riwaka, and those are like, totally my favourite hops, man. It's just, righteous, y'know?

Acid Test. A brand new series from Brothers Beer where we play with all things sour and fruity. 

Red and Green Kiwifruit from the Bay of Plenty, Yuzu from Japan, a Berliner Weisse base. We use the wild Lactobacillus that grows naturally on the outside of wheat malt. This gives you more complexity. More funk. More flavour.

Pucker up.

Made for the Smith's NZIPA Challenge, we decided to go full noise this year. Get lost backstage. Crank that baby up to eleven!

Goes to Eleven is chock-full of Amplifire Riwaka, both in cryo hop pellet and Fresh Hop Oil form.  Add some Cryo Sauvin, and some frozen Sauvin and Nectaron Fresh Hop cones for good measure.

Goes to Eleven. (It's one louder, see.)

Good News, everyone! Studies show that 78 of women prefer men with dad bods. So, there's no reason to drink those sad, lifeless low-carb fizzy water things, when you could be drinking this bad boy!

Packed with Mosaic & Citra cryo, Nectaron, AND Motueka Hop Flakes, you can dive right into this juicy, full calorie beer, knowing that all the while, you're making yourself more attractive to the fairer sex*.
Life is too short to drink low carb.

*Ladies, don't listen to us. It's just a marketing ploy. You can totally drink this beer. It's, um, slimming? Yeah, that's it. Visibly reduces wrinkles.

I can bring you in warm, or I can bring you in cold. About 8-10 degrees ideally, in a nice Beervana glass...

It's cold as Hoth out there! Time for a big, hearty stout to warm your cockles. Roasted Barley, Chocolate & Crystal malts, real Vanilla and toasted Coconut.

At 10, it hugs you like a Wookiee. 

This is the way.

Everyone remembers Nirvana: just three fresh-faced young brothers, making innocent, infectious bubblegum pop, with perfect three part harmonies.

Or something like that. Our memories are a bit hazy. Like this Triple IPA. Which is also hazy, but has another perfect three part harmony - Citra Cryo, Mosaic Cryo, and Nectaron giving you tropical fruits, citrus, even a little bit of that bubblegum. 

The hits just keep coming.

Mmm-Hop.

"Come all without, 
Come all within,
You've not seen nothing like 
The Mighty Quinn"
-Bob Dylan

We don't know what he was drinking  when Dylan penned this song about a charismatic Eskimo (his words. It was a different time) that was going to come and save us all, but it was probably pretty strong stuff. Like this Quintuple, yes Quintuple (!) Hazy IPA:  chock-full of cryo hops - Nelson, Motueka, Mosaic, Citra and Nelson Hop Flakes too. Should have you dancing about like a beatnik in no time.
A blend of no less than three vintages of coolshipped, spontaneous, barrel-fermented wild ale, bottled and further conditioned for a minimum of 12 months.

This Flemish-style Red-Brown Ale is the second iteration of Russet. We brew the same recipe each year and allow it to mature in oak before blending. For this batch, we selected barrels from two different brewing years—2021 and 2023—which had been aged in a mix of ex-Pinot Noir and ex-Pinot Noir Port barrels and inoculated with our house Flanders mixed culture.

Brewed in the traditional Belgian way, this wild ale is made from a grist of 40% raw wheat and 60% malted barley,  using a turbid mash, aged hops, and an extended boil. The wort is then cooled overnight in an open coolship,  allowing wild yeasts and bacteria to inoculate it naturally. After spontaneous fermentation, the beer is matured in  oak barrels for at least one year before being refermented on sour cherries and peaches. It is dry hopped with  Mandarina Bavaria prior to packaging. 
From brew day to packaging, the entire process takes around two years. 
Karamu wild ale is ready to enjoy after approximately four months of bottle or keg conditioning. While delicious when  young, it will continue to evolve and drink beautifully for many years.

This is the second batch of Siege of Liège, a Barrel-aged mixed fermentation saison, initially fermented with French saison yeast, pumped into two oak puncheons with Liège sirop (Wallonian syrup made from pear and apple), and Brettanomyces, Pediococcus, and Lactobacillus, for 18 months. Rich and tangy with a slight sweetness, fennel, pear and big oak.

Brewed in the traditional Belgian way, this wild ale is made from a grist of 40% raw wheat and 60% malted barley,  using a turbid mash, aged hops, and an extended boil. The wort is then cooled overnight in an open coolship,  allowing wild yeasts and bacteria to inoculate it naturally. After spontaneous fermentation, the beer is matured in  oak barrels for at least one year before being refermented on Pinot Gris skins. 
From brew day to packaging, the entire process takes around two years. 
Karamu wild ale is ready to enjoy after approximately four months of bottle or keg conditioning. While delicious when  young, it will continue to evolve and drink beautifully for many years.

While low in alcohol, Light Owl has been brewed to maximise personality.  Chinook hops bring a distinctive pine aroma which is rounded out by the citrus, floral flavours of the Taiheke® hops. The result is a full-bodied, big character Pale Ale despite the low ABV.

column3: Cassels Fogged Up Hazy Pale Ale
column4: Fogged Up Hazy Pale Ale has been created by our award-winning brewers to deliver a full flavoured yet elegant beer.  Juicy tropical fruit notes combine with punchy hop characteristics to bring you a balanced and refreshing brew that will have you coming back for more!

Our Pilsner showcases the very best of New Zealand ingredients. Motueka and Nelson Sauvin hops bring lime and sauvignon grape flavours, alongside subtle juniper berry characters. This is balanced out by the mostly Pilsner malt-base, which provides cracker-like flavours and sweetness, perfectly complementing the crisp, refreshingly bitter finish.

The only thing better than a Cassels Milk Stout... A Cassels Nitro Milk Stout! The secret? Nitrogen. Unlike regular carbonation, nitrogen creates tiny bubbles that give this stout its extremely velvety and creamy texture. Each sip is rich, silky and jam packed with flavour – bittersweet chocolate, dried fruits and bold “coffee-and-cream” aromas. Soft roasted-malt bitterness keeps the sweetness in check. An absolute game changer for stout lovers!

This delightfully fruity, aromatic beer gets its lead from the abundance of USA hops.  A top fermented ale style, the tropical fruit salad and passion fruit flavours give way to a soft, clean, bitter finish.  A very well-balanced beer.

The Nectaron® hop from NZ Hops brings intense tropical fruit aromas to the party.  Hopped at multiple stages through its brewing journey, the toastiness of the NZ Ale Malt and Cassels' House Ale Strain then mellows out all the hoppy goodness and the result is one almighty brew.
Our Red IPA is vibrant and copper-coloured, with a rich, tan head. Prominent pine-needle and citrus hop aromas lead to bold

Lusciously creamy on the tongue, this imperial strength Milk Stout is stronger and sweeter than its Milk Stout sibling. You can expect the same full-bodied mouth-feel and bittersweet, mocha aromatics but with a hint of spice from the Moutere and Willamette hops.  We've also gone one better this time round and paired this delicious brew with Nitro!  Nitrogen creates tiny bubbles that delivers an even silkier and creamier mouthfeel if you can believe it.

Clean, crisp and super refreshing. This lager takes its inspiration from the American Lagers that leave you wanting more. A light whirlpool addition of Mosaic adds a hint of hoppiness to an otherwise traditional drop.

We are bringing back an old Choice Bros classic. This is a Red IPA, packed full of ginger that brings in another element to what is already a punchy style. Piney, citrusy and a strong red malt backbone, this beer does it all
Smoothie Sours have taken over the USA by storm. There is a good reason for that. 40 of this beer is pure fruit puree and you can tell. If big fruity flavours are your thing. This is the beer for you
column6: Mango, Strawberry and Cream Smoothie Sour

column4: Space Cowboy is Choice Bros biggest beer. It's known for the passion fruit flavour that is imbued into the Kohia Nelson hops and paired with the classic Mosaic. So we have taken that, doubled the dry hop rate and fermented it with passionfruit to really level this bad boy up.
The viognier grapes come through as an aroma of apricot, honey and cinnamon. Strong bodied, deep sour flavour with an aromatic wine finish to taste

We took 50 L of high proof rum and aged it in 4 char oak barrels, after we skinned and zested a lot of limes and aged the skins in the rum. All of this was added to a vibrant and punchy stout with some ginger to create the flavour of a Dark 'n' Stormy
The ideal companion for celebrating life’s moments, all whilst keeping your wits about you and waking up feeling refreshed AF
The best selling in New Zealand for a hot minute now. Balanced perfectly with sweet and the right amount of spice. Made to refresh!
New, and launching fresh at Beervana 2026 is our Pineapple Ginger Bear. 4% and fresh off the press!
NZ Hopped pale ale from our mates at Station Brewing.
Hoppy + Fruity. Brewed by our mates at Station Brewing.

After a couple of years on the circuit and enough questions about making it  a permanent fixture, we came up with this. Based on the classic dark & stormy but the our Ginger Bear and a dash of rum. Goes well anywhere!
New recipe for this year. 6% perfection for the cold, fireside or just a good time
Created by blind luck and pitched to the ski slopes for ski lap rewards. Made since 2017 and still a mountain favourite!

Plain and simply put, if you want a beer but are being 'good' for whatever reason, you don't want to be drinking some rubbish hop water.Meet TinyKen. TinyKen is as innocent as the Milkman saying hi to mum; meet your real daddy of Non Alc Hazy IPAs.

Flavours: American Ale, wheat and oats collaborate with Lallemand LoNa yeast to give more body and keep it like a proper beer. Whirlpool Hops balance the malt sweetness with a touch of bitter for that traditional IPA like balance. Big amounts of dry hopping with Mosaic and Freestyle Hop's Hop Kieff smash in flavour and aromas.

If you have been wanting something BIG on Flavour but small on ABV, meet our NEW Little Hazy Pale Ale from our TINY Series. We started with TINY Mammoth and after developing the recipe a bit we have landed on TINY Terror, a 2.3 Hazy Pale Ale that drinks like...

Flavours: Little ABV doesn't mean little on our hop flavours. We are looking at BIG refreshing notes of mango, tropical fruits and citrus balanced with oats for a bit of body!

You wanted an easy-drinking Lager and we are giving you one. Introducing the ‘classic’ beer you've been searching for. Quality meets easy goin’ beer. No more sacrificing your standards.

Flavours: Your standard go-to lager but with the quality ingredients you would expect from DVB! Think crisp, clean, approachable.

Smooth Operator Cream Ale is a light 19th-century American style brew designed to keep you coming back for more. Complete with a slight touch of whole bean vanilla and New Zealand’s finest honey. Think creamy, smooth and refreshing with a clean and zesty finish.

Flavours: Flavours	Lager, Pilsner or Pale Ale Drinker? Welcome to your new favourite style. Some get 1950s Cream Soda…

Split the D takes the Irish dry stout you know and gives it the treatment it deserves. Drawing on Dagda and his endless cauldron, this is our ever‑flowing well of stout done properly – tight, roasty, and built for repeat pints rather than gimmicks.

Flavours: Ale malt, flaked wheat, roasted barley, patent malt and a smidge of Eclipse Wheat build a roasty‑toasty backbone with smooth coffee and dark chocolate notes. Fuggles and Lallemand Nottingham keep it classic – earthy, clean and dry – with a firm bitterness and crisp finish. On nitro it settles into a dense creamy head over a lean, drinkable body: a modern take on a timeless pint.

Does what it says on the tin, mate! Everything you like from a hazy: full flavour, juicy, and all of those delicious tropical notes from dry hopping, without too much bitter.
Flavours: Quenching tropical fruits, citrus and lime zest from the US and NZ hops with solid body to match from oats and wheat

The EXPATRIATE is an American Pale Ale leaving the homeland in exploration of something more. It had no idea it would find New Zealand but the hops were too good to pass up. An alliance of US and NZ hops are sure to enlist your palate for a second round.

Citrus, tropical, floral & pine notes from the hops with a light biscuity malt profile.

Ten years of Double Vision Brewing, and we are stripping it back to celebrate! For our decade milestone, we wanted a proper birthday drink that encapsulates the DVB essence in one drop: a classic, sessionable NZ Pilsner built to celebrate with. The character on the can might be keeping things completely bare, but this beer is fully dressed in the best hop profile we could muster. Accessible, inclusive, and built for repeat pints as we toast to ten years of pushing the boundaries.

Flavours: New Zealand Pilsner malt and a measure of wheat keeps the mouthfeel delicate yet soft, letting the hops take centre stage. Fermented clean with Froth Vagabond Czech Pilsner lager yeast, this brew takes you on a three-stop hop tour. Local Kohatu brings fresh tropical pineapple, Australian Galaxy exudes lush passionfruit, and USA Krush Cryo delivers a final punch of tropical fruit cocktail, berry and bright citrus—snappy, dry, and maximum moreishness.

A Red Rascal lives in us all, sometimes big, sometimes small. Though sometimes dormant, never extinct. A playful nature canned into a drink. Perfectly balanced with bitter and sweet, your Monday to Sunday delicious treat.

Flavours: Fresh, fruity, Gooseberry and citrus with a gentle Red Malt flavour balance.

Targeting systems upgraded. Armour plating reinforced. Standing on the other flank of our third Pacific Hop instalment is Jaeger - Unleashed. After trading blows through Origins and our Fresh Hop clash, this precision-engineered mech has been completely rebuilt with advanced lupulin weaponry to face down the mutated Kaiju. Running a drier, sharper, and cleaner West Coast profile, this unit is locked, loaded, and ready to strike.

Flavours: A clean, bright base of pilsner malt, wheat malt, and dextrine malt, with a touch of light crystal, keeps the body lean, snappy, and light on its feet. Clean Froth Buddy ale yeast lets the hops fire on all cylinders. Nelson Sauvin and Taiheke are supercharged by a heavy drop of Tropical Fusion Kief, delivering sharp, defined notes of crushed gooseberries, white wine grapes, and zesty grapefruit with a clean, punchy bitterness

The beast has broken its chains. Following the raw power of the Origins first set and the seasonal chaos of the Fresh Hop second drop, Kai Juice - Unleashed arrives as the third evolution of our jungle giant. We have taken our wild, nature-powered hazy and mutated it with high-spec hop tech - packing it with concentrated kief and enriched hops to go head-to-head with its metal rival, Jaeger. It is soft, thick, and fully unleashed.

Flavours: A high-protein grist of pilsner base malt, wheat malt, and flaked oats builds a silky, pillowy body with a rock-solid stable haze. White Labs WLP008 yeast cradles a heavy payload of Galaxy, Nectaron, Riwaka Amplifire, and Riwaka Kief. Expect a massive, saturated punch of sweet peach, pineapple, and passionfruit, backed by a heavy wave of dank tropical citrus and fresh-squeezed lime oil.

Don't let the sweet smile fool ya – Dreamsicle's got a bite! This Tropical Orange Creamsicle Smoothie Sour takes that classic orange and vanilla ice cream flavour, then gives it a monstrous twist with a tropical kick. It’s smooth, sweet, and dangerously drinkable, just how we like to nudge those recipe boundaries.

Flavours: Expect a luscious, creamy body from milk sugars and coconut, backed up by a pillowy mouthfeel from wheat and oats. Vibrant orange and guava lead a tropical charge, while banana adds a sweet undercurrent. Smooth vanilla delivers that nostalgic creamsicle hit, but watch out – this flavour combo has a playful, zesty bite that keeps things interesting.

In a world where purple dinosaurs sing sweet songs, I Love You reveals a cheekier reality - sometimes love bites back. This pink-purple sour is like a can of cake: you can have your love for your mate and eat them too! It's your ticket to a tropical sunset escape, blending borderline Theropodic Vibes with fruity indulgence that's far too easy to devour. Looks like Barney will be having both cans for himself.

Flavours: Loaded with barley, wheat, and oats for a smooth base, it's piled high with guava puree, raspberry puree, banana puree, and passion fruit puree for vibrant tropical layers. Coconut, vanilla, and milk sugars add creamy sweetness, while beetroot brings vivid pink-purple colour. The result is a plush, smoothie-like body delivering juicy berry, stone fruit, and citrus, finishing tart and refreshing like a sunset sorbet.

This Belgian Tripel is a bold, scandalously traditional classic that refuses to play it safe, holding onto its secrets tighter than a blowing robe on a windy Wellington day. This monk isn’t going to reveal everything until you get it into your glass to breathe a bit. Dry, effervescent, and stronger than it tastes, it is a decadent, high-gravity, relaxed adventure.

Flavours: A straightforward, 100% European Bestmalz Pilsner malt base is lightened with clear candi sugar to keep the body dry and dangerously drinkable at 9.1% ABV. Fermented with WLP530 Abbey Ale yeast, it delivers a deep, spicy ester profile of cherry, plum and pear, while late additions of bitter dried orange peel bring a bright citrus lift. Mild, delicate Saaz hops linger in the background, providing a soft floral touch and a clean bitterness to balance the sweetness.

Crowning the trilogy, Monarch - Unleashed descends as the ultimate mediator. After watching Kai Juice and Jaeger clash through Origins and Fresh Hops, this colossal triple hazy has had the safety limiters completely ripped off to enforce supreme order. Wielding a massive arsenal of Superdelic, Mosaic, and Clayton Hops’ Amplifire Motueka, this heavy-gravity overlord is built to overpower every other beer in the fridge.

Flavours: A massive, bold grist of pilsner base malt, wheat malt, flaked wheat, and flaked oats is smoothed out with dextrose sugar and maltodextrin for a thick, velvety body that balanced the 10.2% ABV. White Labs WLP008 yeast carries a saturated hop payload of Superdelic, Mosaic, Amplifire Motueka, and Motueka Kief. Expect a sweet-and-dank explosion of red fruit, candy, tropical mango, and fresh-squeezed mojito lime oil that takes you straight to boss level.

Santa may be a Lost Clause, but you're on the nice list if you've got this beer in your vessel. Down here, Christmas lands in summer - so while the big guy’s stuck halfway down a chimney, you can unwrap a sun-season sipper that’s all Christmas cake with no fireplace required.

Flavours: A plush barley-and-wheat base carries rich muscovado molasses, toffee, and dark caramel. Festive spice - cardamom, cinnamon, nutmeg, and ginger - builds gingerbread warmth, while dates and raisins layer dense dried‑fruit notes (fig, plum, sultana). Full‑bodied, smooth, and gently warming, with a long, cake‑like finish.

The After Party has arrived. Bursting with pawpaw, mango, and banana added before and after fermentation, this mega-fruited smoothie sour beer is stacked with tropical goodness and just the right balance of sweet and tangy. Thick, juicy, and ready to keep the party going long after everyone else has gone home.

Back with our spicy sidekicks Apostle. We’ve taken inspiration from the magic of Saint Isidore. Passionfruit & pineapple bring a tropical party, habanero throws the heat, & a hint of mint keeps it fresh, all on top of a smooth corn & barley base. Tangy, vibrant, with just the right kick. Like a blessing with a bit of bite!

A slice of nostalgia in a beer glass. This ice cream sour beer is bursting with bright, tangy lemon curd, layered over a buttery, crumbly pie crust, and finished with fluffy clouds of sweet meringue. Tart, creamy, and shamelessly dessert-inspired. Nana would probably ask for a second pour.

Sometimes you just need a juicy throwback! To quench that craving, we present Mango Grapefruju. An ice cream sour inspired by the classic treat. Bursting with refreshing mango, grapefruit and lime, and rounded out with a soft touch of vanilla for that creamy, frosty finish. Ooh, ahh. It’s gonna hit yah!

In the 23/24 summer, a harvest of deliciously juicy apricots arrived from the southern reaches of Cromwell. We aged them with two funk brothers named lactobacillus and brettanomyces and the result is perfectly funky, lightly soured, earthy, fruity, and bright. It's a wild ride
The Duncan’s waffle maker is back at it. A beer packed with tart raspberries, drizzled in rich maple goodness, and finished with a smooth hit of vanilla.

Warning: May ruin ordinary beers forever.
We've taken our Boysenberry & Apple Crumble Pastry Sour, turned it into a slushie, then floated it on our Maple Peanut Crunch Imperial Pastry Stout. Because self-control is overrated.
column6: Slushie Float (Pastry Sour + Imperial Pastry Stout)

column4: This wild ferment was a Hawkes Bay mission. Broken van, stranded staff, grapes fermenting where they shouldn’t… it nearly broke us. But out of the chaos came something special; a wild sour brimming with funky Brett character, tannish Malbec grapes, and a crisp, clean finish. Proof that hard work (and a little madness) really does pay off.

A wonderfully drinkable interpretation of a classic English ale. Bookbinder is a blend of four malts combined with two classic Nelson grown European hops (Fuggles and Riwaka).

The beer pours an attractive reddish brown, with a cream coloured head. Bookbinder has a sweet, perfumey, malt and hop aroma with a soft, malty, fruit and vinous palate that is both full flavoured and refreshing with a long, gently drying finish.

Apples have a symbolic status in many legends, folklores, and traditions. They can represent love, beauty, wisdom, immortality, and temptation — to name but a few. We just reckon they make a deliciously refreshing beverage. And Juicy Apple Cider is certainly that, with the crisp, sweet hit of ripe apples, balanced by a slightly dry finish. Hmmm, maybe they were right about the temptation thing

One of New Zealand’s first new generation pale ales and now something of a classic, Emerson’s 1812 is all about balance. Pouring a bright amber hue beneath a deep cream coloured head, the aroma hints at caramel and dark toffee balanced with a light citrusy fruitiness.
Medium bodied, the palate first offers a
marmalade-like combination of ripe citrus and caramelised malts before resiny hops come to the fore and lead into a lingering dry finish

Pride of the Plains. First brewed on 16 May 1995, with Saaz D hops (now known as Riwaka), our 2026 reboot has been inspired by the original single-hop recipe. It has the same bold fruit flavours, and notes of passionfruit and lime. Make the most of it, it might not be around again for another 30 years..

It’s unwise to make sweeping generalisations about Phantom Lords. They’re not all sinister and evil. In fact, this one is quite the fun, fruity character. Brewed with a heady combo of Kohatu (NZ), and Mosaic (US) hops, Phantom Lord Hazy IPA is full of complex tropical flavours. Pineapple, lime, and stone fruit, meet mango, citrus and berries. Just watch out, at 6.66, it does still have a bit of devil in it.

This Phantom Lord’s soul draws its spirit not from the Underworld, but California, USA. As a West Coast IPA, it’s absolutely brimming with Centennial, Simcoe, and Citra hops. We were going to stop adding them, but the devil on our shoulder told us to keep going. And he was right. The result has the classic, bitter bite you want, with big grapefruit, resinous pine, and passionfruit undertones. It’s our loudest Phantom Lord yet –– well, it is American.

Brewers Guild of New Zealand Trophy Winner for Stouts and Porters 2016

It displays all the classic stout, characteristics. Black as tar, opulent roast and chocolate notes yet hopped in the way we would hop an American Style Pale Ale.

The malt grist is made up primarily of ale, roast barley, chocolate and crystal malts, with rolled oats included to add that smooth mouth feel.

Phantom Lord has been mash hopped, first wort hopped, hopped in the kettle and once boiled, the steaming hot wort has been pumped through fresh, new season hop cones – hop backed!
A bold, malt-forward stout bursting with rich roasted flavors and a punch of Citra and Simcoe hops — the bigger, bolder sibling of Phantom Lord! Ruler of all things dark and hoppy.
Whisky Barrel Aged Stout - turned into a Soft Serve.

Good game. Crisp golden NZ pils, crafted to showcase the new Hāpi Research trial hop variety NZ04. Canterbury barley with a light touch of toffee malt bring fresh baked baguette sweetness, balanced with clean bitterness, upfront grapefruit citrus and tropical passionfruit notes. Too ez.

The hopocalypse is upon us. Our Dankest Daze, West Coast IPA, brewed with a killer line-up of Chinook, Centennial, Citra and Nelson Sauvin. A crisp, clean malt base, bursting with bright grapefruit citrus and dripping dank hop resin, all finished off with a delicious bitter bite. You can run, but you can't hide. Brewed in collaboration with PikPok, creators of Into the Dead: Our Darkest Days, as part of our Kiwi Game Studio collab bundle, celebrating creativity and innovation in the New Zealand games industry.

Paranormal containment failure detected. Open a portal to a new dimension of flavour. Antebeer, Coconut Ube Smoothie, it’s beer but not as you know it. Strong base blended with purple ube powder, coconut cream, banana, lychee and vanilla for an outrageously colourful, full flavoured paranormal smoothie beer experience that's out of this world. Brewed in collaboration with Deep Field Games, creators of Abiotic Factor, as part of our Kiwi Game Studio collab bundle, celebrating creativity and innovation in the New Zealand games industry.

column3: Boss Level - Bonus Level w/ Blood Orange
column4: All your bases are belong to us. Ready player 1 - you’ve unlocked the Bonus Level. It’s a can load of weaponised hop firepower with a wicked citrus twist. Five different US hop varieties, 100 IBU’s and a massive malt grist to match, finished with a powerful blast of distilled Blood Orange extract. Game over man, game over!

The fog’s rolling in. It’s getting late, time for a Last Cast? Unfathomably lush, hazy Oat Cream IIPA, brewed with a boat load of oats and full cream lactose, then double dry hopped with Mosaic, Motueka, Dolcita and Riwaka for an incredibly smooth mouthfeel and huge tropical fruit and citrus flavour. Dive into its hazy depths, but beware what lies within! Brewed in collaboration with Black Salt Games, creators of DREDGE, as part of our Kiwi Game Studio collab bundle, celebrating creativity and innovation in the New Zealand games industry.
Whiskey barrel aged stout infused with cacao nibs and liquorice root.

ager, Lager, Lager what more can i say. so clean and refreshing just what you need to cleanse the pallet.

Not enough words for this delight. Rich smooth and creamy, decadent with a beautiful warming you will want to savour.
Brewed with 100% NZ hops and malt for a truly local take on a German classic. Expect that crisp, classic lager snap, soft floral notes, and a gentle hint of citrus.
Zesty and refreshing. Made by us, with real ginger and lemon juice. Semi dry.
Juicy and full bodied NZ hazy pale ale, with big tropical notes of pineapple and passionfruit, peach and ripe citrus. Hops - Nelson Sauvin, Nectaron, Motueka, Superdelic.
On hand pull.  Aromas of toasted malt, chocolate and caramel, and a hint of spice from the small addition of rye malt. Medium bitter not overly sweet.

Get your caramel latte fix — in beer form. This rich and creamy oatmeal stout is conditioned on locally roasted Martinborough Coffee beans, lactose and caramel, delivering smooth roasted coffee flavours with a touch of caramel sweetness. Served on nitro for an extra velvety finish.

Soft and light malt background from lager, pilsner, oats and chit malts.
Strata and Superdelic Hops bring notes of strawberry, melon and pineapple with a hint of coconut.

column3: You Must Be This Big To Ride
column4:
You're confused because it's a session double IPA. Nah, you're confused because it's Beervana and a three metre tall fortune teller machine is talking at you. 
This beer is also a magic trick in that it gives full double IPA flavour with just a 4 hit. Amarillo, Ekuanot and Waimea, so it's all citrus and tropical with resin and guava. 
The name reflects our collective childhood memories of fairgrounds etc. You could choose to see it that way and not necessarily as a reference to the 1988 Tom Hanks vehicle.

column3: I Get To Be On Top
column4: For God's sake guys you did it you named a beer after the one scene in the movie I was trying to gloss over what the hell is wrong with you why can't you just make a 5 fruited sour and call it "Mean Fruited Sour" or some shit I mean it's got guava and passionfruit so call it "Guava Sour" or "Passionfruit Sour" and there that's done, we got there without retraumatising the punters it's not difficult

Yep, okay. We're definitely running with that as the name? Nice. I feel like the Tom Hanks theme is distracting us here, but whatever, I used to play Zork and D&D, I'm down with it. 

Ahem: In the cavern of the... evil wizard... the eternal battle between Saaz, Wai-iti and native NZ "Wilding" yeasts... uh... begins anew. And hence a great Saison is... um, unleashed. Upon the land.

Verily, the mists of time have parted. 
Verily, the future stands revealed: it's a West Coast Pilsner and yea, it is crisp and refreshing. 
Verily we have used Simcoe, Citra, Ekuanot and Riwaka, so verily it doth taste of citrus, resin and passionfruit, bright and sharp and excellent. 
Verily, we are milking the Big theme a bit too much by this point.

You remember this one. We made it years ago - a double IPA with Centennial, Simcoe and Sabro. Lots of pine and citrus, deep yet refreshing. 
We often work an 80s retro vibe so we named it after the 1988 Tom Hanks comedy. You know, the one with the dodgy plot in which - never mind. 

Anyway, the beer. I think maybe we were thinking it was a one off but it  turned out really good so we kept making it. And making it, and making it. So here we are, it's Beervana ’26, Big is our centrepiece, and it’s bigger. We have a sick Zoltar machine. We have a whole line-up with names referencing the Tom Hanks movie. And I’m going to come up with tasting notes for every single one.

Maybe you didn't know that this is what you wanted. Well no take-backs. Zoltar has searched your soul and determined that instead of world peace or an end to social media disinformation you actually just want a strong hazy with Nelson Sauvin, Motueka and Simcoe. It tastes of grape, lime and tropical fruit. Maybe a little pine too. 

Mistrusting the soul's true desires is a central theme of Andrei Tarkovsky's 1979 film Stalker, a quiet masterpiece of Soviet-era science fiction and a much better film than Big.
Rich dark chocolate and toffee layered with freshly roasted espresso, finishing smooth, creamy and exceptionally sessionable.
Juicy tropical fruit and bright citrus with a refreshing hazy finish. Light-bodied, low in carbs and packed with flavour.
Pine, citrus and delicate floral aromas lead into a medium-bodied IPA with bold New Zealand hop character, balanced by a firm, refreshing bitterness.
White peach, ripe mango and passionfruit, layered with bright citrus, fresh lime zest and a clean grapefruit finish. Crisp, dry and low in bitterness.
Rich cocoa, toasted coconut and fresh raspberry layered over smooth caramel, with a full, silky body and a long, decadent finish.

Just because something is small doesn't mean it won't pack a punch. The little, delicate, dried flowers of the hibiscus plant are a case in point as they lend a pungent, fruity character, and deep pink colour when added to beer. The same can be said of Petit Luna. Hibiscus, kaffir lime, spicy Belgian yeast, and lactic tartness all brew up to a big refreshing blast of flavour fired by a light, low alcohol beer.

Inspired by our ancestors who travelled across the seas to forge a new life in this land we set about brewing a full bodied strong London style bitter. We combined New Zealand Ale Malt, two different crystal malts, a little wheat, tangy English Goldings and Fuggles hops with our fruity English Ale yeast to create a sociable, sessionable taste of the old country.

North End Salty's Pilspresso In collaboration with Salty's Roastery, we've layered their first-ever roast into this pilsner to bring together the best of both worlds. Coffee was hot side extracted for 10 minutes, followed by a 24 hour cold conditioning stage at 8°c, allowing the coffee aromatics to integrate seamlessly with the crisp pilsner profile. Sweet espresso, subtle toasted grain and a clean crisp finish.

For hundreds of years brewers in the German state of Saxony produced tart, salty, spicy wheat beers called Gose. The style was all but extinct when new world craft brewers discovered it and started to brew versions with increasingly off the wall flavourings. We decided to do something revolutionary and brew a Gose using only the traditional ingredients of water, malt, hops, salt, coriander seeds and yeast. Fruity, tart and just a little salty, we think Become the Ocean is the perfect match to a plate of shellfish

Super Alpha is a hoppy refreshing Pacific Pale Ale that uses the crisp tartness of wheat malt and a blast of fruity New Zealand hops to create a crisp refreshing beer.  Super Alpha takes its name from an unusual variety of New Zealand hop that gives the beer its trademark lemongrass character. The ultimate end to a summer’s day.

North End Core Range You'd often catch Basil at the Hill Road lookout, scoping out his next fishing trip. Peering through the mist and glimpsing a hazy horizon - the inspiration for this brew. This tin cracks open with passionfruit and mango, layered with tropical citrus. Smooth and juicy, with a pithy, balanced bitterness.

Inspired by the wild iron-rich beaches of the west coast we devised a smooth warming stout that combines oats, caramelized rye, and chocolate wheat malt with our fruity English yeast strain and some lightly zesty Nelson hops. The result is a stout fit to fortify against wild west coast winter storms and the perfect match to a night beside the fire. Smooth, rich stout. Fruity notes with layers of chocolate and coffee.

Our American style India Pale Ale started out as a collaboration with a legendary brewer from Oregon in the North West United States. We took the American IPA style and substituted American varieties of hops for New Zealand grown ones. We have tweaked the recipe and made it our own. Piney, grippy and citrus laden.

Big, punchy aroma with a heap of grapefruit, stone fruit, tropical & pine. A lot like Supercharger, but hoppier.
Notes of pineapple, papaya, nectarines, citrus and melon. Juicy and soft bodied, with some bitterness in the back end. Using Motueka, Cascade Mosaic & Eclipse hops.
Packed full of passionfruit, white-grape, tropical, pine & citrus.This beer combines classic kiwi hop flavour with some more modern, fruit-forward hop expression. Soft & juicy, yet resinous & punchy.

Big, punchy aromas of grapefruit, tropical fruit and pine lead the charge, followed by layers of dankness and sweet fruit. A lean malt base lets the hops shine bright, while a firm bitterness cuts cleanly through the finish.

A complex and mix of raisin, coconut, vanilla, chocolate aromas and flavours. Some bourbon booziness, oak tannins and a hint of balsamic acidity add to the impact and complexity of this enticing beer.
Bursting with tropical, citrus, passionfruit and white-grape flavour. Fresh, punchy and delicious. Everything you like about Quickchange, but more of it!

Tantalise your taste buds with this refreshingly complex kettle soured ale. Brewed with the traditional process, which gives acidity to the beer, the incredible fruit taste comes from the beer being fermented with a crazy amount of fruit juice. We've paired a tart citrus burst of lime juice with the sweet, tangy flesh of pineapples to create a refreshing and fruity ale.

column2: Good George Distilling x Pink Boots NZ
column4: Combining all that is GOOD! Pink Boots and Good George Distilling Lemon Myrtle, Makrut Lime Leaf and Rosemary gin is paired with a classic soda. Think Citrus Bomb without all the fruit getting in the way.

A nose full of tropical fruit straight out of the gate. This ‘new squeeze’ is not afraid to make itself known. The hazy nature lures you in with intrigue and leaves you with beautiful mouth feel and a palate full of tropical fruit and citrus.
Kicking off a (fingers crossed) winning season for the Cleveland Browns with caramel, chocolate malt notes and a lightly spiced American hop character.

Twofold x Pink Boots Collaboration for International Women’s Day. 
Brewed on a bed of NZ-grown German-style pilsner malts and Light Lager, hopped with scrummy Riwaka from Clayton Hops and the latest Pink Boots Blend, flown fresh from the hop press by Yakima Chief. This year’s blend features Ekuanot, Centennial, HBC 638, and Mosaic.
Expect crisp, clean malt backbone with tropical and stone fruit notes, bright citrus, and a touch of resinous pine

Bright and unexpected, Rudi’s Butterfly Lime Cider blends zesty lime with a hint of floral flair. Brewed with butterfly pea flower, it pours a subtle blush that deepens with citrus - an enchanting visual twist. Lightly tart and ultra-refreshing, it finishes crisp and dry. This is Rudi with a wink - colourful, cool, and cheekily unconventional.

Sessionable and award-winning, Rudi’s Lager is a super clean, crisp New-World brew featuring Dr Rudi hops – named after the man himself. Nelson Sauvin adds lift and character, striking a bold balance between a firm slap to the face and a warm embrace. Thirst-quenching – bloody refreshing – it’s lager the Rudi’s way: no fuss, all flavour.

Our award-winning New Zealand Pilsner showcases the distinctive character of local hops, delivering a fuller body with layered flavour. Clean, crisp, and mid-dry – it strikes a perfect balance between subtle malt and the vibrant lift of four NZ hops: Dr Rudi, Motueka, Nelson Sauvin, and Kohatu. A modern classic with a proudly Kiwi soul.

Rudi’s IPA bursts with bold American Simcoe hops, layered with the unique complexity of New Zealand varieties. Expect vibrant notes of tropical fruit, pine, and a hint of passionfruit. This punchy yet balanced brew finishes lush without overwhelming the palate. A confident, hop-forward IPA that’s refreshingly bold, smooth, and unmistakably Rudi’s.

Our Hazy Pale Ale showcases the vibrant character of New Zealand hops in a smooth, juicy pour. Bursting with tropical fruit, citrus, and a touch of white grape – it’s brewed with Dr Rudi, Motueka, Nelson Sauvin, and Kohatu. Soft on the palate with a gentle haze – bold, fruity, and effortlessly drinkable from first sip to last.

Unfiltered, and irresistibly juicy - Rudi’s Double Hazy is a bold hop bomb wrapped in velvet. It pours a glowing golden haze crowned with creamy foam. Aromas erupt with mango smoothie, ripe peach, passionfruit, and citrus zest. The mouthfeel is pillowy, thanks to oats and wheat. Saturated yet smooth, it’s Rudi unleashed - cloudy, confident, and dangerously drinkable.

Zesty hard ginger beer, little bit sweet, little bit ginger, little bit refreshing.

Handpull - Inspired by the legendary Lembas bread of Middle-earth, this collaboration with Choice Bros Brewing takes the idea of bread and turns it into beer.
A soft, hazy pale ale with a distinctly bready and biscuit-like character, complemented by a gentle touch of vanilla. Malt-forward and comforting, with a creamy texture and just enough sweetness to evoke the rich, sustaining character of the Elves' famous travelling bread.
A beer made for journeys, adventures, and second breakfasts.

Golden, glowing, and godlike, this easy-drinking beer is pure Queenstown charm in a pint. Brewed with Nelson Sauvin and Pacific Jade hops, it opens with soft malt, a hint of toffee, and the feeling of morning sunshine over a green pitch. With biscuit notes, subtle bitterness, and a full-bodied “can-do” attitude, Queenstown Draught tastes like weekend sport, mountain air, and local pride refreshment built for legends.
Handpull - Orange marmalade, earthy notes and toffee biscuit with a soft, balanced bitterness.

Naturally unfiltered and bright straw in colour, this beer showcases Ella hops with soft citrus and floral aromas. Light and dry on the palate, it delivers gentle grapefruit pith flavours and a smooth, balanced bitterness.
Crisp Pilsner meets brut-style bubbles: bright, bone-dry, and refreshingly sparkling, Using noble German hops and a touch of NZ Riwaka, fermented with lager and wine yeast .

A rich and velvety stout brewed with plum and sake from Zenkuro. Deep roasted malt, dark chocolate and coffee notes meet juicy plum, subtle vanilla and a gentle sake character, finishing smooth, warming and beautifully balanced.

A big, juicy hazy packed with Motueka, Riwaka, and Nelson Sauvin hops. Bursting with tropical mango, guava, and citrus aromas, it’s full-bodied, creamy, and loaded with that unmistakable hazy goodness.

A bold West Coast IPA bringing together the punchy character of US hops with a bright NZ hop edge. A sturdy malt base gives the beer a rich deep-gold colour and a touch of chewy malt sweetness, providing balance against a firm bitterness and generous hop load. Aromas of ripe stone fruit and dank pine resin lead into a subtle citrus undertone, with the US hops taking centre stage while the NZ varieties add brightness and lift. Full of character, bitter, resinous and built for hop lovers.

A bold Belgian-style Tripel with a modern hop twist, brewed with Citra, Nelson Sauvin and Hallertau Blanc. Bright, clear and golden with a soft white head, it opens with aromas of citrus, peach and subtle clove. Flavours of citrus, stone fruit and honey follow, supported by classic Belgian fruity esters, gentle spice and a warming character. It finishes dry and clean, with a light, balanced bitterness.
Aussie style pale ale with a classic passionfruit and citrus flavour.
Flavours of tropical fruit, coconut with a touch of candy character.
Bright citrus and pineapple character .
Complex tropical, white wine and peach notes.
Dark fruit, fig and raisin with a classic Belgian spice character.
Freeze distilled weizen doppelbock to showcase an intense banana malty sweetness with a silky smooth finish.
Dark chocolate, rum and vanilla with toasted coconut.

Far away in England an art forger called James Edward Little specialised in forgeries of Maori and Pacific art, even though he’d never been near our neck of the woods. He fooled a lot of “experts” and consequently Puke Ariki has the biggest collection of Little Fakes in the world.

This session IPA deceives by fronting big Amarillo and Mosaic without the alcohol kick.

This Belgian inspired Sour Beer is a blend of two mixed ferment beers, a 12-month Chardonnay barrel–aged ale and a 24-month bourbon barrel–aged ale. After blending, the sour ale was pitched with Brettanomyces yeast and bottle conditioned for four months, adding layers of complexity and funk to the barrel character and balanced sourness. 
 
The finished beer is beautifully complex. Notes from the Chardonnay barrels are clearly present but never overwhelming. Malt character provides balance and length, leading to a moreish, satisfying finish.

Dicky Barrett, renowned for being as wide as he was short, became somewhat of a hero around these shores. Lovingly given the moniker Tiki Parete by local iwi, he fought alongside his Māori brothers against the cowbell-ringing enemy from the north.

Legend has it he died from injuries while battling a whale, but other reports state a botched double bypass may have been the cause. In honour of Dicky’s girth, this English Bitter boasts a full body, balanced with herbal Antipodean hops.

Served on Handpull.

"Sick as, bruh" meant something different for New Plymouth's surfers back in the day. It was probably what they were telling their General Practitioner after paddling through the proverbial let go from the town's 'revolutionary' sewerage system installed in 1933. Thankfully, things have been cleaned up since then, allowing for a much more refreshing ocean experience at the surf break known as 'Bogworks', located directly outside our Brewery.

A combination of clean, light malts and crisp Riwaka hops make this New Zealand Pilsner the perfect way to cap off a day catching the big ones.

Back in the day, Whare Matangi, estranged son of Ngarue, was given a magic dart, or tara, that would lead him to his father. After a few throws the tara hit Ngarue’s house at the mouth of the river. The place became known as Te Whai-tara uni-a-Ngarue, or Waitara.

Our own Magic Dart aims for an American-style golden ale with a combo of US and kiwi hops combining sweet stonefruit and tropical aromas.

The impressive brains in the natural gas industry once came up with a genius solution to a dangerous problem. The problem? Natural gas doesn't have an odour and hazardous leaks were going undetected. The solution? Skunk Juice!

What is Skunk Juice you ask? It's a pungent brew of Sulphide and Methyl Mercaptan that can be smelled almost three kilometres from its source. It pongs so bad, it once shut down the town of Stratford for a whole day!

Our version of Skunk Juice harnesses a hazy chemical brew of Mosaic and Citra hops, that unlike its namesake, gives off a beautiful tropical and citrus aromas, so you'll always know when someone nearby has poured themselves a glass of Skunk Juice!

column3: Black Doris Plum Sour Ale - Oak Barrel Aged
column4:
This Belgian inspired Sour Beer is a mix of 12 and 24 month old mixed ferment Oak Barrel Aged Ales rested on crushed Black Doris Plums and then conditioned in bottle with fresh Brettanomyces yeast.

Store upright in the fridge for at least 24 hours before gently decanting.

Limited to 1200 wax dipped and hand labelled bottles, and one festival keg exclusively for Beervana 2026.

column3: Raspberry Sour Ale - Oak Barrel Aged
column4:
This Belgian inspired Sour Beer is a mix of 12 and 24 month old mixed ferment, oak barrel aged ales rested on raspberries picked from Windermere Berry Farm in Whanganui, and then conditioned in bottle and keg with fresh Brettanomyces Yeast.

BREWERS NOTES:
We found a blend from four different barrels that we thought would match perfectly to the sweet tang of Raspberry. We blended the beer in tank with the fruit and let it re-ferment for four months before bottling with priming sugar and a fresh pitch of Brettanomyces yeast. The beer itself is earthy, funky and tart with a big fresh punch of the iconic Raspberry, and vivid colour.

column3: Flemish Bruin Ale - Oak Barrel Aged
column4:
Smooth, complex, and beautifully balanced, our Flemish Bruin pours a deep mahogany with ruby highlights, crowned by a wispy, off-white head. On the nose, it opens with inviting aromas of dark cherries, dates, and a hint of balsamic, intertwined with gentle oak and a complex earthiness. The malt base boasts notes of caramel and toffee, quickly met by a bright, tangy acidity that adds lift and vibrancy.

A hint of oak lingers in the background thanks to nearly 24 months of careful maturation. The finish is dry, slightly tart, and refreshingly clean, leaving you ready for another sip. Perfect for slow sipping by the fire reading a leather bound dictionary, pairing with rich meats, or matching with aged cheeses.

In 1969, backing the arts in New Plymouth was enough to get you spat on in the street. Then-president of the Operatic Society, John Murphy, copped some ill-directed spray while fighting to save the Opera House from demolition. Thankfully, it wasn’t curtains after all, with Murphy’s efforts helping ensure the Showplace lived on — and continues to host world-class productions to this day.

This West Coast IPA celebrates 100 years of the New Plymouth Operatic Society with a proper ensemble of old-school and modern hops. Pine, citrus and tropical resin take centre stage atop a lean malt base, creating a brew that hits like a standing ovation on closing night.

column3: Feijoa Sour Ale - Oak Barrel Aged
column4:
This Belgian inspired Sour Beer is a mix of 12 and 24 month old mixed ferment, oak barrel aged ales rested on freshly picked Feijoas from Oakura Farms Orchard on Ahu Ahu Road, and then conditioned in bottle with fresh Brettanomyces Yeast. column3: Vintage Stout 2024 - Pōkeno Whisky Barrel Aged
column4:
The 2024 Vintage Stout is the sixth release of our ‘Vintage’ range of yearly Barrel Aged releases.

This Imperial Stout was brewed with a ‘Reiterated’ Double Mashing schedule, in which the second mash is mixed in with high gravity Wort from the first mash. This process allows us to extract a more concentrated sweet Wort, which feeds the yeast to create a higher alcohol brew.

A small addition of dextrose sugar in the fermenter added an extra hit of alcohol which gives this beer a warming balance to the oak tannins. We then decanted the beer into New Zealand Whisky Barrels from Pōkeno Distillery, and left the beer to rest for nine months.

The process of Oak ageing creates a chemical reaction between the wood and the beer, in which flavour compounds such as tannins and vanillins leach into the beer, creating a rounded and complex flavour. By treating the oak barrel as an additional ‘ingredient’ we’ve been able to create this complex and rich brew that is perfect for winter nights, and will also cellar extremely well as it gains complexity with ageing.

A bold lager that captures the essence of Japanese "umami". Inspired by the clarity and refinement of Japanese cuisine, this lager delivers a light, smooth drinking experience with a deep sense of umami.

Featuring the fresh and vibrant aroma of NZ Riwaka hops, the refined character of sake yeast, and the rich umami of traditional Japanese ingredients such as Kombu kelp, Shiitake mushroom, and bonito flakes bring depth and lasting complexity.

Brewed in Japan by Japanese brewer Kengo Saito, who learned his craft here in Wellington, this NZ IPA is a homecoming of sorts.
Bright and citrus-forward, with vibrant aromas of orange and grapefruit layered over the fresh, green character of New Zealand hops. Tropical yeast notes add depth, leading to a flavorful, refreshing IPA with a clean and satisfying finish.
Born from Kengo’s time in Wellington, brewed in Yokohama, and now back in New Zealand.

Captured the delicate "umami" of Japanese green tea in a beer. Blending three carefully selected teas and using an optimal cold-steeping method, we bring out deep umami and a lingering finish. Brewed clean and simple, with gentle malt and hops that elevate the elegance of the tea. Japanese green tea takes the spotlight.

UTSUROI deliberately brings the ginjo-like aromatics of sake yeast to the forefront. The aroma is reminiscent of Japanese sake, with expressive notes of ripe melon and pear. 
Rice koji, polished rice bran, and wasanbon sugar contribute soft, layered umami, giving the beer a delicate yet complex depth. To further explore umami as a defining element of Japanese food culture, we also used Kombu kelp, bonito flakes, and Shiitake mushrooms.
The result is a clean, refined beer with a quiet, savoury finish that continues to unfold long after each sip.
